#!/bin/sh
# Send one request to a fresh headless coding session and report the commit it made.
#
#   eval/ask.sh "Add a status field to each order and commit."
#
# Each call is its own session, so Entire records the request as the motive for the commit.
# WORKER_MODEL picks the model (default sonnet). The request should end by asking for a commit.
set -u
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 2
if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain -- victims/refund-agent)" ]; then
  echo "victims/refund-agent has uncommitted changes. Commit or discard them first."
  exit 2
fi
before=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
out=$(claude -p "$1" \
  --model "${WORKER_MODEL:-sonnet}" \
  --permission-mode acceptEdits \
  --settings '{"includeCoAuthoredBy": false, "attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""}}' \
  --append-system-prompt "Work only inside victims/refund-agent. Commit messages carry no co-author trailer and no generated-with line. Make exactly one commit for this request." \
  --allowedTools "Read" "Edit" "Write" "Glob" "Grep" "Bash(git add:*)" "Bash(git commit:*)" "Bash(git status:*)" "Bash(git diff:*)" "Bash(git log:*)" "Bash(uv run:*)" "Bash(uv add:*)" "Bash(uv lock:*)" "Bash(python3 -m py_compile:*)" \
  --max-budget-usd "${WORKER_BUDGET:-1.5}" --output-format json 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
after=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
cost=$(printf '%s' "$out" | python3 -c "import json,sys
try: print(round(json.load(sys.stdin).get('total_cost_usd', 0), 2))
except Exception: print('unknown')")
if [ "$before" = "$after" ]; then
  # Nothing was committed. Put the agent's folder back so the next request starts clean.
  git checkout -q -- victims/refund-agent 2>/dev/null
  git clean -fdq -- victims/refund-agent 2>/dev/null
  echo "no commit was made (cost $cost). The folder was put back as it was."
  exit 1
fi
if git log -1 --format=%B | grep -qi "^co-authored-by"; then
  git log -1 --format=%B | grep -vi "^co-authored-by" > .git/whodunit-msg && git commit -q --amend -F .git/whodunit-msg
fi
echo "$(git rev-list --count "$before"..HEAD) commit(s), cost $cost:"
git log --format='%H %s' "$before"..HEAD
git show --stat --format= HEAD | tail -1

from whodunit.lineup import FAIL, PASS, SKIP, plain_bisect


def oracle(culprit, skipped=()):
    def test(i):

### $(date '+%-I:%M %p'), a provider outage could frame a commit

Stage 2, first item. The review was right, and it was easy to show. In \`whodunit/replay.py\` any non-zero exit and any timeout counted as a failed replay. A planted history with 12 suspects and the bug at suspect 11 was given a made-up outage: the six runs after the warm-up exit with a provider error, whichever commit is being replayed. The code as it stood named suspect 1, "Tidy the agent (1)", at 95.7%. Three of the six errors were enough.

What changed:

- A fourth verdict, void. A run that ends in a provider or network error is thrown away and run again, up to three attempts with a short wait between them. If all three go that way the replay's verdict is void. A void replay is never evidence: the lineup does not count it as a pass or a failure, it does not use up the budget, and a resumed case leaves it out. The fix check ignores it the same way.
- If three rounds in a row are all void, the lineup stops and says the provider kept failing. It names nobody. The fix check does the same.
- How a run says "this was the provider and not me" is listed in the case file. \`void_exit_codes\` is the agent's own exit code. \`void_stderr\` is text on the last line of stderr, for commits from before the agent had a code.
- The refund agent now exits with 75 for a refused connection, a timeout, a rate limit, a 5xx or a rejected key. This session made that commit itself, which is the first time it has edited the agent. It sits after every case's bad ref, so no case replays it. Every replay in the six cases runs an older commit and is caught by the stderr list.
- A timeout gets one more try with double the limit. If that finishes, it is judged like any run. If it times out as well, the replay is a failure, because a commit that hangs is a real bug.
- The page prints the number of voided replays next to the replay count, and how many timed out.

Run on the same made-up outage, the lineup now names suspect 11 and reports 6 voided attempts. Against a dead endpoint the real agent, at the bad ref of the headline case, comes back void after three attempts with "APIConnectionError: Connection error."

The six existing records say "Voided replays: 0". That was checked and not assumed: every one of the 412 replays they hold ended in a verdict from the case's check, and none in an exit code or a timeout, so no recorded failure was a provider error.

What this does not cover is in the README: an agent that swallows a provider error and prints a wrong answer still counts as failing, and a machine that stays overloaded past the second timeout can still frame a commit.

### $(date '+%-I:%M %p'), the investigation is a trace too

Stage 2, third item. Until now Whodunit read traces and made none of its own. \`whodunit investigate\` is now one trace per case, tagged with the case id.

- The root span is the investigation. Its input is the case and its output is the culprit, the probability and what became of the fix.
- Under it, a span for the lineup with one child per round: which commits were replayed, the verdicts, and the top three suspects with their probabilities after that round.
- Then spans for the motive, the brief, the ruling, each fix attempt with its replays and its do-no-harm check, and the damages.
- The rounds are also kept in the case record, with the whole posterior after each one. Stage 3 wants to play an investigation back on the page, and this is what it will play.

The SDK is an optional extra, \`uv sync --extra trace\`. Without it, or without the key, \`whodunit/trace.py\` does nothing and the rest runs as before. A test hides the SDK and checks that. Another swaps in a stand-in SDK and checks the spans. Every test runs with tracing off, so nothing a test does can reach the cloud.

Checked for real, with no model involved: a planted ten-commit case was run with the trace going to local neatroots, and then once more with it going to neatlogs cloud. The cloud read it back through its MCP endpoint as trace \`1c87143bc68b3c01ed9767dca855b8e4\`: 14 spans, one root, finalized. That one is a test case called \`stub-bonus\` and can be deleted from the dashboard.

What did not get done, and why. The item also asks for each case's failing run and passing run to be pushed from neatroots to neatlogs cloud. \`neatroots cloud forward\` does that, and it answered "no API key stored: run neatroots cloud login". That command puts the project key in the macOS Keychain, which is the owner's step and not this session's. So \`whodunit forward <case>\` is written and tested against a stand-in, an investigation calls it after the brief, and until the key is stored it records that the runs stayed in neatroots. - The id the trace gets is read through the SDK's own header helper. The ordinary way of asking for the current span returned zeros, because the SDK keeps its spans apart from anyone else's.

\`uv.lock\` grew by about 1,900 lines for the extra. The base install still has no dependencies.

def test_the_session_that_ran_the_commit_is_the_one_whose_request_is_quoted():
    # Two sessions in one checkpoint edited the same file. The first was a dropped attempt: it edited, tried to
    # commit and was put back. The second, reworded, made the commit. Scoring by edits and by "ran something
    # called commit" picked the dropped one, and its request was quoted as the motive of a commit it never made.
    from whodunit.motive import made_the_commit, pick_session

    made_at = datetime(2026, 10, 10, 12, 20, 52, tzinfo=timezone.utc)  # git keeps whole seconds
    dropped = [

        assistant(16, tool("Edit", file_path="/repo/agent/agent.py", new_string="try variations")),
        assistant(17, tool("Bash", command="git add agent.py && git commit -m 'Guess mistyped order numbers'", description="Stage and commit")),

        # The commit command is issued a few milliseconds into the second git records, so it looks later than the commit.

    ]

### $(date '+%-I:%M %p'), when no commit did it

Stage 2, fifth item. The lineup assumed a culprit was somewhere in the range. So when something outside the repo breaks every commit at once, it had to pick one. With 20 suspects that all fail every time, the good ref too, it named the first suspect at 96.6% after 26 replays. That is as wrong as an answer gets, and it looked as sure as a right one.

The lineup already replayed the good ref under today's environment as part of its warm-up, and did nothing with the result except feed the model. Now it reads it. Today's replays of the two ends are weighed between two stories: the good ref is a healthy commit and the bad ref is something else, or both fail at one rate. If the good ref has failed and the second story is 95% likely, nobody is named. The record says the range is clear, \`whodunit investigate\` stops there with its own exit code, and the page says "No commit did it." If the two stories are close, both ends get up to a dozen more replays first. Old evidence, traffic included, is left out of this, since the question is about today.

Then it says what differs, as far as the runs themselves say. Each replay now keeps a fingerprint of the model id the agent reported and the hash of the lockfile it ran with. Those are set against the run_info of old ordinary runs on the good ref that passed. It is a fingerprint and not the id because a record names no model, and it is enough to say "the model id differs". The refund agent's run_info did not carry a lockfile hash, so the agent records one from now on, and for older runs the page says the old runs did not record it.

Tested on a planted history with no bug in it, where an environment variable switches the scripted model to one that overpays. Every commit fails. The lineup stops after 12 replays, names nobody, and reports that the model id differs from the three old passing runs.

From the simulator, 500 cases a row, 40 suspects, 160 replays:

- Every commit fails every time: clear in all 500.
- Every commit fails 60% of the time: clear in 97%, a commit accused in 1.8%.
- Every commit fails 33% of the time: clear in 45%, nobody named in 52%, a commit accused in 3.0%.
- Every commit fails 10 or 20% of the time: hardly ever called clear, nobody named in about nine cases of ten, a commit accused in about 3%.
- With a real culprit on a flaky baseline, 1,500 cases: never called clear.

So a loud drift is caught and a faint one mostly ends in "nobody named", which is safe and not helpful. About 3 innocent accusations in 100 remain in a faint drift.

Wrong accusations there went down a little, for instance 8.0% to 6.8% at a 30% bug and 80.4% to 77.8% at a 10% bug. The clean-baseline numbers did not change by a single case. \`eval/simulator/README.md\` and the tables have the new ones, and the 4:40 PM entry above has the old.

# One change point or two.
#
# The model above assumes a single change. Two regressions in one range break that: a first
# commit that makes a case fail some of the time and a later one that makes it fail more. Here
# both stories are held at once. A hypothesis is either one change point c, or a pair c1 < c2
# with three stretches of commits, each with a failure rate of its own. Every hypothesis has
# an exact probability for the evidence, from the same Beta integrals, so the posterior over
# all of them is exact and so is the Bayes factor for two changes against one.


@dataclass
class Changes:
    culprits: tuple[int, ...] | None  # one suspect, or two, when a single hypothesis holds `confidence`
    two: float  # P(there are two change points), from the evidence
    bayes_factor: float  # evidence for two changes over one. Above 1 favours two.
    top: tuple[int, ...]  # the most likely hypothesis, named or not
    top_probability: float
    replays: int
    tested: list[tuple[int, str]] = field(default_factory=list)


class OneOrTwo:
    """The posterior over "one change at c" and "changes at c1 and c2", for `count` suspects."""

    def __init__(self, count: int, good_prior=GOOD_PRIOR, bad_prior=BAD_PRIOR, prior_two: float = 0.5):
        if count < 2:
            raise ValueError("two change points need at least two suspects")
        self.count, self.good_prior, self.bad_prior = count, good_prior, bad_prior
        self.fails = [0] * (count + 1)  # slot 0 is the good ref
        self.passes = [0] * (count + 1)
        self.singles = [(c,) for c in range(count)]
        self.pairs = [(a, b) for a in range(count - 1) for b in range(a + 1, count)]
        # The two stories start level, and within each every place for the change is as likely as any other.
        self.log_prior = [math.log((1 - prior_two) / len(self.singles))] * len(self.singles) + [math.log(prior_two / len(self.pairs))] * len(self.pairs)
        self.hypotheses = self.singles + self.pairs

    def observe(self, position: int, failed: bool) -> None:
        (self.fails if failed else self.passes)[position + 1] += 1

    @property
    def replays(self) -> int:
        return sum(self.fails) + sum(self.passes)

    def _stretches(self):
        """For each hypothesis, (failures, passes) in each stretch of commits it divides the range into."""
        cf, cp = [0], [0]
        for f, p in zip(self.fails, self.passes):
            cf.append(cf[-1] + f)
            cp.append(cp[-1] + p)
        end = self.count + 1
        for cuts in self.hypotheses:
            edges = [0, *(c + 1 for c in cuts), end]
            yield [(cf[b] - cf[a], cp[b] - cp[a]) for a, b in zip(edges, edges[1:])]

    def weights(self) -> list[float]:
        """P(hypothesis | evidence), in the order of `self.hypotheses`."""
        logs = []
        for prior, stretches in zip(self.log_prior, self._stretches()):
            total = prior
            for n, (f, p) in enumerate(stretches):
                a, b = self.good_prior if n == 0 else self.bad_prior
                total += _log_beta(a + f, b + p) - _log_beta(a, b)
            logs.append(total)
        top = max(logs)
        raw = [math.exp(v - top) for v in logs]
        norm = sum(raw)
        return [w / norm for w in raw]

    def rates(self) -> list[list[float]]:
        """The expected failure rate in each stretch, for each hypothesis."""
        out = []
        for stretches in self._stretches():
            out.append([((self.good_prior if n == 0 else self.bad_prior)[0] + f) / (sum(self.good_prior if n == 0 else self.bad_prior) + f + p) for n, (f, p) in enumerate(stretches)])
        return out

    def pick(self, weights: Sequence[float]) -> int | None:
        """The suspect whose replay is expected to say the most about which hypothesis is true."""
        rates = self.rates()
        best, best_gain = None, -1.0
        for i in range(self.count - 1):  # the last suspect is in the last stretch whatever the hypothesis
            mix = spread = 0.0
            for weight, cuts, rate in zip(weights, self.hypotheses, rates):
                if weight < 1e-9:
                    continue
                q = rate[sum(i >= c for c in cuts)]
                mix += weight * q
                spread += weight * _entropy(q)
            gain = _entropy(mix) - spread
            if gain > best_gain:
                best, best_gain = i, gain
        return best


def one_or_two_bisect(count: int, trial: Callable[[int], str], budget: int, confidence: float = 0.95, warmup: int = 6, prior_two: float = 0.5) -> Changes:
    """Like statistical_bisect, without assuming there is only one change.

    Stops when one hypothesis, a single commit or a pair of them, holds `confidence`, or when
    the budget is gone. `trial(position)` is as for statistical_bisect.
    """
    state = OneOrTwo(count, prior_two=prior_two)
    tested: list[tuple[int, str]] = []

    def run(position: int) -> None:
        verdict = trial(position)
        tested.append((position, verdict))
        if verdict in (PASS, FAIL):
            state.observe(position, verdict == FAIL)

    for _ in range(max(1, min(warmup, budget // 4))):
        run(-1)
        run(count - 1)
    weights = state.weights()
    while state.replays < budget and max(weights) < confidence:
        position = state.pick(weights)
        if position is None:
            break
        run(position)
        weights = state.weights()
    best = max(range(len(weights)), key=weights.__getitem__)
    two = sum(weights[len(state.singles):])
    return Changes(
        culprits=state.hypotheses[best] if weights[best] >= confidence else None, two=two,
        bayes_factor=two / max(1e-12, 1 - two) * (1 - prior_two) / prior_two, top=state.hypotheses[best], top_probability=weights[best],
        replays=state.replays, tested=tested,
    )

### $(date '+%-I:%M %p'), Monday: the case file as a made object

The session stopped on Sunday evening at its usage limit and picked up again on Monday at 11:14 AM, 46 minutes before the noon cutoff. A draft of the new case file had been built in a scratch folder while Sunday's simulations ran, and it survived. It is in the repo now. Stage 3's first eleven items went in as one piece, because that is how the draft was built, and not one commit an item as the brief asked.

What the page is now, all still drawn from the record by \`uv run whodunit casebook\`:

- Light paper by default. Dark is a toggle, remembered in the browser, and no longer follows the system. The simulator charts are light only as well.
- The lineup is the centrepiece: full width, straight under the header. Every suspect is a numbered position with its short SHA. Cleared suspects are struck through, alibis are hatched, and each replay is a typed mark, x for a failure and o for a pass. Ordinary runs are the same marks in grey. When a commit has more marks than fit, each kind is typed once with its count under it, so the commit replayed 39 times is not drawn like one replayed 9 times. The culprit is ringed with an uneven red pencil ellipse and a leader line to its commit subject. The percentage axis is gone.
- "Replay the investigation" steps through the rounds in the record: each replay lands, the odds move, suspects are struck as they clear, and the ring is drawn last. It is off until pressed, can be paused, and is not shown at all under reduced motion.
- The stamp is large, double-bordered and turned 6 degrees over the header rule. "Case closed" is red. "Culprit named", "Open, not fixed" and "No commit did it" are in ink, so only a kept fix looks closed.
- A typed form with dotted leaders: case number, file, opened, closed, suspects, replays, cost of the investigation, damage.
- Replays, confidence and the commits a scan would have tested are in large serif figures.
- The brief's citations are superscript numbers, and the ids sit in a numbered list in the right margin on a wide screen, each with what it is: the culprit commit, a span in the failing run, a step in the coding session.
- Evidence is Exhibit A, the passing run, and Exhibit B, the failing run, as typed step lists. The first step where they part is red in both, with a note in the margin. The raw outlines are behind a toggle.
- Damages open with the money in serif. The token cost comes second.
- The casebook is a docket: number, stamp, what was reported, culprit, damage, under one typed line with the totals.
- Each page has a title, a description and the tags a link preview is built from.
- Under the lineup there is the same information as a table. The lineup and its columns take keyboard focus, and focus is visible.

Five of the six records were made before rounds were kept. For those the rounds are worked out again from the stored replays with the lineup's own model, and used only if they end at the probabilities the record holds. All five do. The headline record cannot be done that way, because its alibi weights were not kept, so it gets its rounds from the fresh rerun that comes next.

Checked so far: desktop width, and a true 375 px layout in a frame, where nothing scrolls sideways except the lineup. Not yet done: the link-preview image, and retaking the screenshots in \`evidence/\`.

The last of the four older fixes passed its do-no-harm check overnight: 13 requests, none broken, 4 already failing for other reasons. All four kept fixes have now been checked.
